messages:
Maya (Growth): Quick sync — need final narrative for the benchmark section in the webinar deck by EOD Thurs. Scope: 1) one-liner, 2) 3 chart choices, 3) email subject tests, 4) landing CTA + routing. Can we lock today?
Omar (Product Marketing): On it. Quick note — avoid 'cost per token' jargon in external copy. Use 'dollars per 1k tokens' or 'inference spend' for clarity.
Gaurav (Research): Agree. Pasting the trimmed results from the run (8k context, mixed prompts).
Gaurav (Research): ```
variant,95th_latency_ms,dollars_per_1k_tokens,throughput_rps
redwood-optimized,120,0.85,22
baseline-open,380,1.90,20
alt-quant,160,0.95,21
```
Leigh (Design): For slides I'd recommend: 1) speed vs cost scatter, 2) stacked waterfall of cost components, 3) tail-latency violin (appendix). Which two should be front-and-center?
Maya (Growth): Scatter + waterfall. Violin goes in appendix. We need one headline claim: 'Same throughput, 2-3x cheaper; 3x lower tail latency' — is that defensible with these numbers?
Gaurav (Research): That claim maps to the run above with prefix cache + quantization profile X. Add a short note about measurement conditions.
Gaurav (Research): Measurement details (short): accelerated GPUs, production-like prompt mix, warm KV cache for prefix-heavy flows.
Omar (Product Marketing): Let's avoid naming GPUs in the public claim. Use 'optimized inference runtime' or 'accelerated hardware'.
Samir (Growth Ops): For email subject hooks — A: 'Cut LLM inference costs up to 3x — join our benchmark demo' B: 'Faster responses, fewer dollars: new benchmark walkthrough' C: 'How we halved tail latency for production LLMs' — A/B/C to test?
Maya (Growth): A is punchy, test C as alternate. Keep B as fallback for retargeting.
Leigh (Design): Design note: make the scatter linear X (latency) and log Y ($/1k tokens) so smaller cost diffs stand out; annotate 'real-world prompt mix'.
Omar (Product Marketing): Agree on axes. Adding throughput as a second visual might clutter. If needed, add a small inset showing RPS.
Gaurav (Research): I can produce an inset. Main should be latency vs dollars. Also add callouts: 95th vs median so folks see tail improvement.
Maya (Growth): Action items: Omar finalize the headline + 2 subject lines by Tue noon; Leigh produce two variants of scatter + waterfall by Wed; Gaurav confirm numbers + callouts by Tue EOD; Samir set up email A/C 50/50 and landing tagging. I'll assemble deck Friday AM.
Samir (Growth Ops): Setting up A/C in HubSpot now. Landing page will include a checkbox for 'See Dedicated vs Hosted routing' and we will tag leads with 'bench_webinar_2026'.
Omar (Product Marketing): Draft one-liner: 'Redwood's inference runtime reduces tail latency and inference spend — benchmarks + tradeoffs explained.' Lean?
Maya (Growth): Cleaner: 'Redwood reduces inference spend and tail latency — real benchmarks, real tradeoffs.' Use that as headline unless objections.
Leigh (Design): Uploading rough comps to Figma: <https://figma.com/file/xYZ123> — two color treatments (dark/light) and two annotation styles.
Gaurav (Research): Uploaded CSV and a simple Vega-lite spec to Drive: <https://drive.redwood/bench2026.csv>. Use the 'redwood-optimized' row as the primary callout.
Maya (Growth): One more ask — add a tiny footnote on methodology: 'Benchmarks run on production-like traces; see appendix for fullconfig.' We'll draft the appendix text after numbers are locked.
Omar (Product Marketing): Will add copy for appendix.
Samir (Growth Ops): FYI — routing rule on LP: if user selects 'Dedicated', tag for sales outreach. If not, route to self-serve onboarding.
Maya (Growth): Great. If no blockers, locking narrative Thurs EOD. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
